findings.evidence: Workout prescriptions, History/More, Add set and timer actions retain a similarly subdued green-gray treatment. Library previews and counts use the same muted tier. All are readable, but task instructions and actions are less immediately distinct than exercise names and entered values. This prior objection remains.
findings.userConsequence: Reading the prescription and finding secondary logging actions requires closer attention during a workout.
findings.suggestedChange: Strengthen task-relevant secondary text slightly, especially prescriptions and timer actions, while keeping optional catalog previews subordinate.

findings.evidence: The Body card now has a visible Edit label, but the Alex Morgan identity row still ends with a small, faint pencil alone.
findings.userConsequence: Editing the profile name is less discoverable than editing the other profile fields, and the control treatment is inconsistent within the page.
findings.suggestedChange: Use the same pencil-plus-Edit treatment beside the identity row.

findings.evidence: The equal-width export fields are clear, but the raw preview wraps session headings and set records across several lines. The metadata preamble occupies much of the visible preview before the first workout, whose heading breaks between the day name and completion status.
findings.userConsequence: Copying is straightforward, but checking the actual workout content remains slower than checking the export scope and counts.
findings.suggestedChange: Provide a compact readable session preview above expandable raw text, preserving the complete copied and downloaded content.

strengths: Onboarding clearly distinguishes the current step, later actions and the manual builder alternative.
Prompts makes Copy prompt prominent and explains the external AI chat and return-to-Import workflow.
Import recovery, exercise resolution and confirmation communicate distinct next actions. Confirmation explains the saved Squat link and optional further review.
All three exercises' entered set values are visible above the mobile workout footer. The earlier accessory-set visibility objection is resolved without sacrificing readable values.
Routine overview selects Week 2 and marks Lower body as Next workout. Plan: Draft is consistent between list and overview.
History rows now have separators and chevrons. Sorting labels and export filters are clear.
Desktop navigation and content placement are consistent across all four captures. Routine Open is grouped within a shorter span.
Workspace exposes theme choices with the correct visible selection in both themes, prioritizes backup and distinguishes destructive import.
Profile supplies weight dates, actual values and point markers. The builder explains unfinished routines, and the session summary has a clear next action.
The prior requests to invent a warm-up rest duration or remove Skip day are not supported by a visible usability failure in these captures.
limitations: Opened all 27 manifest files directly with the image-viewing tool. Every image was readable.
Read findings from all twelve prior reviews, all four prior assessments and the round 04 implementation response. No other current-round output or parent conversation was consulted.
Earlier screenshots were not reopened. Comparisons concern documented prior objections; no direct image-to-image regression claim is made. No new major issue was established.
Contrast judgments are visual only. No contrast ratios or accessibility conformance were measured.
Static screenshots cannot establish keyboard behavior, accessible names, touch target bounds, persistence, data safety or scrolling behavior.
Evidence covers 390x844 mobile and 1280x900 desktop, with four dark screens. Content outside the captured viewports was not inspected.
No source inspection, live app interaction, app mutation, file edits, installation, commits, pushes or delegation was performed.
